## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** no runtime issue found in the reviewed scope. The Tailscale panel now probes the CLI with `omarchy-cmd-present`, which uses Bash `command -v` and ships with Omarchy, so detection no longer depends on the optional `which` package. One optional hardening note for the new test scan follows.

| Condition | Base (`["which", "tailscale"]`) | Head (`["omarchy-cmd-present", "tailscale"]`) |
|---|---|---|
| `which` not installed, `tailscale` on PATH | Probe fails to start; Quickshell emits no `exited`, so `onExited` never runs and the panel does not reach the installed state | Helper exits 0, `installed` becomes true, status refresh starts |
| `tailscale` absent | `which` exits 1 if installed; otherwise the same failed start | Helper exits 1, panel shows "Not installed" |

The base row is derived from Quickshell v0.3.1 `Process` source (a failed start logs and clears the process without emitting `exited`), not from a rendered shell.

**Verified:**
- All three references to the renamed process (`busy`, the `refresh()` guard and the `Process` id) are updated; no `whichProcess` reference remains.
- `omarchy-cmd-present` resolves on the shell's PATH in the supported launch paths. The packaged install places it in `/usr/bin` alongside `omarchy-launch-shell`, and dev-link mode prepends `$OMARCHY_PATH/bin`. Panels already launch other `omarchy-*` helpers by bare name, including `omarchy-tailscale-send` in the same file.
- The PR description is accurate about lock and menu: both already probe with `command -v` and mention `which` only in comments. The Tailscale probe was the only `which` launch in `shell/`.
- The tailscale test fails on base with the head test file, passes on head, and passes with the two changed files applied to the current `quattro` tip (both files are unchanged between the merge-base and the tip).

**Optional test improvement:** in `test/shell.d/tailscale-test.sh`, `rg ... || true` treats a missing or failing `rg` the same as "no match". With a `["which", "foo"]` launch injected and `rg` removed from PATH, the test still printed `ok - shell plugins do not call the which binary` and exited 0. Calling `require_command rg` (already in `base-test.sh`) before the scan, or failing on `rg` exit codes above 1, would make the guard fail closed. The pattern also matches only the exact `["which"` spelling; spaced or single-quoted arrays, `bash -c "which ..."` and `/usr/bin/which` pass it. A broader pattern, or describing the guard as covering the argv form, would match the PR description more closely.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of head `643a827b` against merge-base `9c5482c5` and the `quattro` tip at `d201fb95`, including Quickshell v0.3.1 `Process` and Qt 6.11.2 `QProcess` source for argv and PATH resolution, and Omarchy launch and packaging sources. The tailscale test ran in an isolated command sandbox on base, head and tip plus PR, with a positive control, a missing-`rg` case and synthetic PATH checks of `omarchy-cmd-present`. No live Tailscale daemon, rendered panel or desktop session was exercised. Omarchy does not pin a Quickshell version, so the base failure mechanism is stated for the inspected version.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
